chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from whomever mentioned it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Fadl ibn al-Sakan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Recognize God through God, the Messenger through the Message, and the Masters of Authority through their enjoining of good, justice, and benevolence.'

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: Masters of Authority — Quranic term (4:59) interpreted in Shia tradition as referring specifically to the Imams
key_terms.اعْرِفُوا: Recognize, know — imperative plural, an obligation directed at believers
key_terms.الْإِحْسَان: Benevolence, excellence in conduct, doing more than required
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: That which is recognized as good; the socially and religiously approved

ai.seo_question: How do we recognize God and the Imam according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of Imam Ali (AS) establishing three epistemological principles for recognizing divine authority: God is known through His own self-disclosure, the Prophet through the content of his revelation, and the Imams (Ulu al-Amr) through their practical qualities of enjoining good, justice, and benevolence. This hadith is foundational to Shia theology, as it grounds the recognition of rightful authority not in external claims or lineage alone, but in observable qualities that align with divine command.
